l01.title: Lesson 1: The alphabet and its sounds

h-sound.title: The sound of г
h-sound.body: A voiced fricative, the voiced partner of х. Phoneticians describe it differently: /ɦ/, glottal, in the published IPA illustration (Pompino-Marschall et al. 2017); [ʕ] before а, о, у, и, е, [ɣʲ] when softened, and [ɣ] before voiced consonants and at the end of a word in Vakulenko 2025, who finds no convincing evidence for glottal [ɦ]. Both agree that it is voiced, which English h is not: Vakulenko finds English h closer to х. The plosive /ɡ/ has its own letter, ґ.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA
Vakulenko (2025), Balcania et Slavia 5(1)

v-allophones.title: The variants of в
v-allophones.body: One phoneme, /ʋ/, with variants by position: labiodental [ʋ] before front vowels, nearer [w] before rounded back vowels, and [u̯] at the end of a syllable, as in був (was, masculine). It does not turn into f. Vakulenko 2025 disputes the label [w], since the lips barely protrude, and writes [β̞].

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA
Vakulenko (2025), Balcania et Slavia 5(1)

y-vowel.title: The vowel и
y-vowel.body: Written /ɪ/ here, following the IPA illustration: retracted and lowered compared with і, with a hard consonant before it. Close to the Russian vowel [ɨ], but not the same sound. Vakulenko 2025 transcribes it as a lowered, advanced [ɨ] instead. Without stress it comes close to е.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA
Vakulenko (2025), Balcania et Slavia 5(1)

o-unreduced.title: о without stress
o-unreduced.body: Written /ɔ/ here, following the IPA illustration. Unlike in Russian, it does not reduce towards a without stress: вода́ is never вада́. It can still shift slightly, towards [o] before a stressed /u/. Vakulenko 2025 describes the vowel as close-mid [o] rather than /ɔ/.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA
Vakulenko (2025), Balcania et Slavia 5(1)

shared-forms.title: One form, several cells
shared-forms.body: Case endings overlap, so one form can fill several cells: кімнати is genitive singular and nominative, accusative and vocative plural, and кімнаті is both dative and locative singular. On this board either slip is right in any of its cells.

sources.title: кімната (English Wiktionary)

soft-hard.title: Soft, half-soft and hard
soft-hard.body: Only the denti-alveolars /t d n s z t͡s d͡z r l/ have a true contrast between plain and palatalized phonemes, as in лад and ладь, or рис and рись. Other consonants become half-palatalized, or "semi-soft", as a variant before /i/ and /j/. Plain consonants are velarized, which is why л is usually dark [ɫ]. The consonant before е and и stays hard.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA
Feldstein, An Approach to Ukrainian Reading for Russian Students

final-voicing.title: No final devoicing
final-voicing.body: Unlike Russian and most other modern Slavic languages, Ukrainian keeps a voiced consonant voiced at the end of a word: віз ends in [z], and ваз differs from вас. Assimilation mostly goes one way: a voiceless consonant becomes voiced before a voiced one, as in о́тже [ˈɔd͡ʒɛ], but a voiced one doesn't devoice before a voiceless one. The exception is г, which becomes [x] before к and т, as in легки́й and ні́гті. In fast speech a final voiced consonant can partly devoice.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA
Feldstein, An Approach to Ukrainian Reading for Russian Students

free-stress.title: Free, moving stress
free-stress.body: Stress can fall on any syllable, can tell words apart, as in доро́га and дорога́, and can move within one word's forms: роби́ти, роблю́, ро́биш. Ordinary writing doesn't mark it, so it has to be learned with each word.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA

apostrophe.title: The apostrophe
apostrophe.body: It stands before я, ю, є, ї, mainly after б, п, в, м, ф, р and after a prefix ending in a consonant, when the consonant stays hard and [j] is pronounced: м'яч, п'ю, подвір'я, в'їзд. Without it, я, ю and є soften the consonant instead: ряд, люк.

sources.title: Є-мова, Українська за 27 уроків (enrolment needed)
Ukrainian alphabet (Wikipedia)

one-sound-two-letters.title: Two letters, one sound
one-sound-two-letters.body: дж and дз are written with two letters but are single affricates, /d͡ʒ/ and /d͡z/: джерело, дзвін. They have no letter of their own in the alphabet.

sources.title: Є-мова, Українська за 27 уроків (enrolment needed)
Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA

iotated.title: я, ю, є, ї
iotated.body: At the start of a word or after a vowel, each is [j] plus a vowel: я́блуко, моя́. After a consonant, я, ю, є soften it and write the vowel: ряд, люк. ї always stands for two sounds.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA
Є-мова, Українська за 27 уроків (enrolment needed)
